source_title: Taylor Swift donated $100,000 to rebuild flood-hit Tennessee playground in 2010
source_excerpt: Taylor Swift, the iconic American singer and songwriter. keeps making headlines not only for her songs but also for the tremendous charity works that she keeps doing. This time, the 14 Grammy winner is again in the news for her charity work for kids. In 2010, when devastating floods damaged a popular playground in Hendersonville, Tennessee, Swift contributed $100,000 to help bring it back to life.Now 16 years later, the playground, known as Kids Kingdom, has returned to the spotlight as the city considers a fresh investment in recreational facilities. It includes an all-inclusive playground and better sports field.In August 2026, Hendersonville officials discussed applying for a grant of approximately $3 million through the BlueCross BlueShield of Tennessee Healthy Place programme. The proposed funding would support an all-inclusive playground at Taylor Swiftâs Kids Kingdom and turf improvements at Memorial Parkâs lacrosse field.This new development has brought renewed attention to a community playground being supported by the singer.What happened in 2010Kids Kingdom was originally built in 1996 as a community-wide project in Hendersonville, a city near Nashville where Swift went to high school. More than 1,500 volunteers reportedly helped construct the original playground. However, the playground's location made it vulnerable to flooding.In May 2010, heavy rainfall caused the Cumberland River to overflow and the water rose to 52 feet. It damaged Hendersonville, where Kids Kingdom was left with serious safety problems.Although the playground had experienced flooding before, the 2010âs was a disaster. As per to playground manufacturer Little Tikes Commercial, Tennessee's parks and recreation authorities considered the facility too dangerous to remain open in its existing condition.The $100,000 donation for the renovation of the playWhile the estimated cost of rebuilding the playground was $175,000, funding constraints threatened to delay the reconstruction work. Swift, who had grown up in Hendersonville, came forward and donated $100,000 for the work. Contemporary reports published in August 2010 confirmed that the singer had donated the money.As per a report by Little Tikes Commercial, her contribution was significant and helped the city bridge the funding gap and move ahead with rebuilding the damaged facility. The donation helped restore a shared community space.In December 2009, she had donated $250,000 to support schools she had attended. She also contributed $500,000 towards flood relief efforts in the Nashville area in 2010, according to local reports.Preserving the playground's identityThe rebuilt playground preserved its castle theme, and colourful structures, spiral staircases and modern play equipment were added. Its distinctive arched entrance was also retained, keeping it original.Plans included plaques recognising the 1,500 people who had helped construct the original facility, along with clay handprints made by children. For Hendersonville residents, the playground represented not simply a recreational space but also a place created through collective effort.Why Hendersonville is considering another investmentThe proposed 2026 grant would focus on making recreational spaces. An all-inclusive playground is designed to enable children with different abilities to play together. Depending on its final design, such a facility can incorporate accessible routes.According to the published summary of Hendersonville's committee discussions, the proposed grant would not require a local matching contribution. However, the funding remained subject to the grant application process, and the available records did not confirm a final award.For Hendersonville, the story of Kids Kingdom has come full circle in an important way. A playground that was built through community participation was severely damaged by flooding, then rebuilt with help from a hometown celebrity.Swift's $100,000 donation helped make that reconstruction possible in 2010. Now, the city's proposed grant application places the same playground at the centre of another effort to improve public recreation.Whether the latest funding bid succeeds remains to be seen.
